newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures close lower on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures close lower on profit taking.

text.p: Profit taking following large gains posted earlier in the week pushed CME lumber futures down for losses after setting a new high in March early.

Further bull spreading, partly from strong cash, kept January supported at times, but the profit taking also weighed on that month. Futures ran up initiallly and posted a new contract high in March early on carry demand from Thursday's limit gains before slipping, traders said.
March set a new contract high of $410.00 per thousand board feet and January rose to its highest level since December 10 before retreating on the profit taking, they said.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $392 per tbf, up $9 from midweek and $6 under last Friday's level. Activity and demand increased as the week unfolded, they said.
Lumber closed $2.10 to $8.00 per tbf lower with January off the least at $405.00 and March off $4.80 at $400.10 per tbf.
